claims.text: Equiatomic FeCoNi has a disordered fcc structure, high saturation magnetization, and low coercivity.
An almost equiatomic FeCoNi composition has configurational entropy of at least 1.0R.
Controlled high-temperature annealing can promote short-range atomic reordering in equiatomic FeCoNi.
Rapid quenching can freeze partial L1₀-like order into equiatomic FeCoNi.
The treatment will create localized nanoscale L1₀-like ordered domains in a predominantly fcc FeCoNi matrix.
Low-symmetry chemical or L1₀ order can enhance magnetocrystalline anisotropy.
Nanoscale ordered regions in treated FeCoNi will act as domain-wall pinning sites.
Stronger domain-wall pinning increases the barrier to domain-wall motion and raises coercivity.
Annealed and quenched equiatomic FeCoNi will have measurably greater coercivity than untreated disordered equiatomic FeCoNi.
The treated FeCoNi alloy will have greater coercivity than the previously studied FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt derivatives.
The coercivity increase can occur with minimal reduction in saturation magnetization.
Rapid thermal annealing increases coercivity in fcc FeCoNiMnCu films through microstructural changes and strain-induced anisotropy that strengthen domain-wall pinning.
Adding Pt to FeCoNiMnCu lowers cubic symmetry and produces an L1₀ phase with high magnetocrystalline anisotropy.
The intervention is effective only while the alloy remains predominantly single-phase fcc with minor nanoscale ordered regions.
Extensive ordering or phase separation can lower configurational entropy below the qualifying threshold and adversely affect magnetic properties.

contradictions.description: The conditions state that maintaining an almost equiatomic composition consequently guarantees configurational entropy ≥1.0R, whereas the boundary states that extensive ordering could lower configurational entropy below 1.0R without requiring a composition change. These statements use composition-based ideal entropy and ordering-dependent actual entropy inconsistently.
